operations.label: Additional formal scope guide
operations.new_html:
Additional formal coverage

P11, P23, P24. Ideal risk and grammar. Nested expectations decompose ideal risk. Summable grammar evidence controls tails. Prior splitting preserves whole-record evidence; predictive consistency also needs the joint-likelihood mixture.

P31, P35, P37. Stochastic identification. Passive laws can miss interventions. Independent reset trials give simultaneous bounds. Observable completion retains experiment coverage, spectral separation and filtering margins.

P46, P47, P48, P49. Curved rotation and learning. The exact rotation requires a Lorentz cone; finite positive generators fail. Polygon approximation has a common-policy budget. Sequential learning retains conditional coverage, initial coverage and summable failures.

P50, P51. Matrix certificates. Injective matrix embeddings and positive congruences certify laws with exact mass and initial coverage. The rotation has an exact witness. Predictive base norm need not equal ambient trace norm.

P52, P53. Continuous instruments. Integrable positive operator densities and exact mass give consistent policy laws and positive-density updates. Reference changes preserve laws. Finite polynomial Gram identities certify the whole interval.

P54, P55. Moment identification. Correct supplied dimension and degree, with an invertible covered core, enable reconstruction. Without the degree restriction, positive rank-one laws share low moments while differing in total variation.

P56, P57, P58. Cells and averaging. Exact bin laws require bin-measurable policies. Positive-cell posteriors average density-weighted updates. Congruence averaging retains covariance. Positive cell averages have base-norm resolution Lh, sharpened to Lh/3 for equal uniform intervals.

P59, P60, P61. Comparison and realization. Common-cone, common-reference models admit full record-law budgets under one common history policy. Observable invertible template matching transports certificates. Realization retains true dimension, degree, domain and initial-state checks.

P62, P63. Oriented curved certificates. Quadratic Gram identities require mass orientation. Exact moments and initial coverage give all-horizon laws. Operator-only geometry discovery is a conditional proposal followed by full-family verification.

P64, P65. Positive polynomial approximation. Actual integral coefficients preserve cone positivity and exact mass without a true-degree assumption. The stated Lipschitz bias, fitted coefficient error and later correction budgets remain separate.

P66, P68. Sequential residual evidence. P66 remains partial for natural-number tests on standard Borel spaces, with recorded transport and rescaling restrictions. P68 gives lower discrepancy evidence conditional on the simultaneous residual event.

All propositions P1-P65 and P68 have complete formal mappings. P66 remains partial in its stated sector. The other 20 propositions retain written proofs without formal mappings.
